group_assessment.weighting: Medical University of Lodz. Two departments appear on the article: Analytical Chemistry (first author) and Molecular Cancerogenesis (corresponding author A. K. Bednarek and two co-authors). NOT independent of the gene's discovery: Bednarek is first author of the WWOX discovery paper (PMID 10786676) and of PMID 11719429, the WWOX cDNA used here came from his own collection, and both sequence motifs the paper relies on are cited to his 2000 paper. This is a follow-up by a discovery author in his own laboratory, not external replication. No orthogonal laboratory has replicated this enzymology in anything the paper cites.

queued.reason: Bednarek 2000 Cancer Res, the WWOX discovery paper. It is the sole source of the two sequence motifs this paper's interpretation rests on (GANSGIG 131-137, YNRSK 293-297) and of the expression pattern used to argue physiological relevance. No receipt in the ledger. Highest-value hop from this reading.
Bednarek 2001 Cancer Res; cited for Golgi localisation requiring an intact SDR domain, a structure-function statement this reading cannot check. No receipt.
Chang 2005 Oncogene; cited as the 17-beta-estradiol activation result the authors call their results consistent with. Already carried as abstract-only in FT-113. No receipt.
Driouch 2002 Oncogene; cited for tumour transcripts lacking the substrate-binding part of the SDR domain, which is the paper's bridge from enzymology to carcinogenesis. No receipt.
Mahajan 2005 Cancer Res; Ack1 phosphorylation of WWOX at Tyr33 and Tyr287. Background only for this reading. No receipt.
Marijanovic 2003 Mol Endocrinol; one of the two clustering analyses placing WWOX with 17-beta-HSD3, the only basis for the regiochemistry this paper never measured. No receipt.

entries.proposition: PANEL READING, Figure 1. Neither SDS-PAGE panel carries a molecular-weight ladder lane or any size annotation, and the paper contains no Western blot, antibody or mass-spectrometric confirmation. The assignment of the induced band to a WWOX fusion rests on expected migration alone.

Panel B: four lanes numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, no marker lane, no kDa labels; lane 1 carries an intense low band, lane 3 a prominent higher band plus a strong mid band, lanes 2 and 4 neither.

entries.proposition: PANEL READING, Figure 2. The empty-vector NusA control is not a blank: it reaches about 0.43 at 340 nm by 30 minutes against about 0.95 for NUS-WWOX, so roughly 45 per cent of the signal is host activity. The GST system behaves differently in absolute terms (about 0.07 control against about 0.47 GST-WWOX), so the two expression systems do not agree in magnitude on the same substrate. Neither panel carries error bars.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Page 76, Figure 2. Panel A y-axis 0 to 1, NUS-WWOX filled markers plateau near 0.95 by 20 min, NUS open markers rise steadily to about 0.43 at 30 min. Panel B y-axis 0 to 1, GST-WWOX filled markers plateau near 0.47 by 15 min, GST open markers reach about 0.07 at 30 min. No error bars on any point of either panel.

entries.proposition: PANEL READING, Figure 3A. Each panel plots four traces defined by an in-figure legend. The NUS-WWOX extract without any steroid still reaches about 0.22 to 0.24 at 340 nm, so a quarter of the signal is substrate-independent. For estrone the empty-vector-plus-substrate trace reaches about 0.80 against about 1.24 for NUS-WWOX, a ratio of 1.55 and the largest host background of all seven substrates, although the Results text places estrone in the group it calls 3- to 6-fold lower than NUS-WWOX. No panel carries error bars.
